# Labs {.unnumbered}

The Computer Lab (Slot FL, 1 credit, 0-0-2) runs for two hours each week:

| Branch | Day | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Electrical | Tuesday | 2:00–4:00 pm |
| Mechanical | Wednesday | 2:00–4:00 pm |
| Materials | Wednesday | 2:00–4:00 pm |

Bring your laptop if you have one. You can also work in the browser with [OnlineGDB](https://www.onlinegdb.com/online_c_compiler) — no installation needed. We will show you how to set up a local C toolchain (gcc/clang) in the first lab.

## Lab Schedule

The schedule below is **tentative** and covers all 11 practical modules of the [syllabus](./syllabus.qmd) (the *module* column refers to the syllabus practical table). Lab handouts are **self-contained**: where a lab reaches a construct before its full lecture treatment, the handout introduces just enough of it to do the exercises. Because institute holidays fall on different weekdays, the Tuesday (EE) and Wednesday (Mech/Materials) batches drift by a week in places — go by the *session number*, not the date.

| # | EE (Tue) | Mech & Materials (Wed) | Topic | Module |
|:---:|---|---|---|:---:|
| 1 | Aug 4 | Aug 5 | Basic input/output programs (incl. toolchain & editor setup) | 1 |
| 2 | Aug 11 | Aug 12 | Conditional statements | 2 |
| 3 | Aug 18 | Aug 19 | `for` loops | 5 |
| 4 | Aug 25 | Sep 2 | `while` and `do-while` loops | 6 |
| 5 | Sep 1 | Sep 9 | Lists and strings: arrays, strings as character arrays | 3 |
| 6 | Sep 8 | Sep 16 | Using libraries (`string.h`, `math.h`, etc.) | 10 |
| 7 | Sep 15 | Sep 30 | Functions and recursion | 7 |
| 8 | Sep 29 | Oct 7 | Tuples & dictionaries, C-style: structures and key–value lookup tables | 4 |
| 9 | Oct 6 | Oct 14 | File handling | 8 |
| 10 | Oct 13 | Oct 21 | Error handling | 9 |
| 11 | Oct 27 | Oct 28 | Problem solving I (GATE / ACM ICPC style) | 11 |
| 12 | Nov 3 | Nov 4 | Problem solving II | 11 |
| 13 | Nov 17 | Nov 18 | Problem solving III | 11 |

: {tbl-colwidths="[6,13,20,53,8]"}

**No lab on:** Wed Aug 26 (Milad-un-Nabi), Tue Sep 22 & Wed Sep 23 (mid-semester exams), Tue Oct 20 (Dussehra), Tue Nov 10 & Wed Nov 11 (holidays).

::: {.callout-note}
The syllabus allocates 28 practical hours (8 of them for problem solving); holidays leave 13 sessions = 26 hours. The remaining 2 hours of problem solving will be covered through a make-up lab session (date TBA) and problems embedded in earlier lab sheets.
:::

## Useful Tools

- [OnlineGDB C compiler](https://www.onlinegdb.com/online_c_compiler) — write, run, and debug in the browser.
- [C Tutor (pythontutor.com)](https://pythontutor.com/c.html) — visualize the step-by-step execution of C programs.
- [Search & sort visualizations](https://www.cs.usfca.edu/~galles/visualization/Search.html) — see linear vs. binary search in action.
- MIT OCW 6.087 [labs and assignments](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/pages/assignments/) — extra practice problems with solutions.
